golden.query: How does the education system make kids feel jealous and ashamed of being less?
golden.answer:
Related, not a direct answer:

"All over the world people of one color hurt people of another color people of one class hate people of another class people of one religion hate people of another religion this is because we have very primitive minds that considers anyone different as a threat. Even at home the older siblings alienate the younger sibling because they're different in age. Research shows that in an atmosphere of stress the brain becomes less friendly towards anything that is different and unfamiliar. That is why social alienation is practiced more in organizations that are very competitive. That is why in times like today when there is a widespread anxiety, communal violence and racial violence have a tendency to flare up. It does not require to be older to understand this. Even young children have gone through the painful experience of alienation at schools and playgrounds. Discrimination and separation is hurtful no matter how you show it. We are the only species on earth that hurts its own species on the basis of skin color or diversity"
— Sri Krishnaji (nUrc8O7Avvk, 61s)

golden.query: Does the pressure to be number one in academics damage a child's inner peace?
golden.answer:
Related, not a direct answer:

"I and Preethaji believe strongly, is the problem of pressure, is the problem of psychological pressure. You, the current generation, are enduring the greatest pressure than anybody else in history. why is this psychological pressure or where is this psychological pressure coming from each and every one of us each and every one of you out there are pressured are feeling pressure peer pressure parental pressure education pressure pressure to look good and beautiful pressure to look intelligent pressure to succeed pressure to make money pressure to be fashionable yes pressure to be trendy absolutely and pressure to win every second of your life you are feeling pressured and this disease or this pressure that you're feeling do you think it will go away do you think you all can be free of pressure there is no way you can be free of this pressure can you ever avoid pressure from your parents can you ever avoid pressure from your friends can you ever avoid pressure from your work impossible you cannot avoid these pressures these pressures are going to be part of your life but you will need to learn to navigate through these pressures you need to learn to make decisions and you need to learn to live your life free from this pressure if you If you can learn to handle this one single thing in your life, you will conquer everything in life. Your life will be beautiful, your relationships will be beautiful, your work will be beautiful, your friendships will be beautiful, everything will be beautiful. If you are not able to handle this pressure, you as an adult, when you are growing up, your life is going to be miserable. There are a lot of adults out there who cannot handle pressure, I am sure you know that very well. You will be seeing that in your home, you will be seeing that amongst your parents, your friends, your relatives, everyone who are not able to handle pressure. And in fact, when they are not able to handle their pressure, whom are they showing it upon? Yes, you, the kids. That is why it is so important that as you grow up, you don't do that same mistake, that you show it on your kids. Are you all able to understand the seriousness"
— Sri Krishnaji (_X5jRvqxEEo, 9s)

golden.query: Why do we try to control the person we love when we feel insecure?
golden.answer:
Related, not a direct answer:

"You will still want people in your life not because you love them but because you fear being lonely. It is like a constant game of you be in my life but maintain a distance, you be with me but don't get too close we are afraid of being wounded and wounding others with our anger. We are scared of our own loneliness and that we will be disappointed with our partners. We as human beings have been on the run from each other. We have been running away from ourselves too. You are terrified you may ruin your own life with disappointments and loneliness. This time of seclusion and compulsive of living alone or with your families can actually help you come face to face with all this."

golden.query: How can I stop suffocating my partner with possessiveness and neediness?
golden.answer:
Related, not a direct answer:

"she says to him what kind of love is this that you have for me? This is not love, this is insanity. She continues, she says, do you think I can satiate your thirst for pleasure throughout my life? Do you think this madness is sustainable? Is this love at all? Her wise enquiry was like a bucket of ice -cold water on his burning fire. He walks away from his wife's house in great pain and anger. Slowly he realizes that his dependence on his wife for fulfilling his craving and longing was making him into a slave, was making him unwise, was making him blind. In fact he was so possessive of her that he gave no room, no freedom, no space. He realizes that his attachment to his wife was an addiction."

golden.query: Why does romantic attachment turn into jealousy and constant suspicion?
golden.answer:
Related, not a direct answer:

"The first reason could be that you have over the years allowed the fire of anger, the fire of suspicion and And the fire of jealousy to grow in you and consume you. Is this your problem? Please reflect and see the truth. There is no shame in ever seeing the truth. It will transform you. The second reason could be that you have a deep hunger to be loved. And you don't know how to fill your heart with love. You have somewhere equated love with control. role and having total authority over the other. You want to own your partner or your children or daughter -in -law like you own a piece of furniture. This is something you must understand. Absolute obedience is never love. It is slavery. Love is only possible between two people who who respect each other. When you hurt a person emotionally and physically, what they feel for you is fear or anger. Love cannot arise in the heart of someone in whom you have put fear. It cannot arise if you have insulted them."
— Sri Krishnaji (bSyewSnu2Ak, 99s)

Related, not a direct answer:

golden.query: In the story of the two monks, what prevents us from dropping past grievances?
golden.answer:
Related, not a direct answer:

"An angry mind is exactly like this monkey's mind. The more you are thrashed by life, the more tightly you will cling on to your anger. Namaste. In rural India, there is a way of catching mischievous monkeys that come to steal from homes. They deliberately leave some very aromatic desserts in a tiny hole in a tree. The monkey gets excited, smelling the desserts, and squeezes its hand through the tiny hole and gets hold of the delicious dessert. But the hole is too small for it to get its closed fist out. The monkey struggles to get its hand out of the hole, but will not let go of the dessert and so is stuck. duck, and the villagers easily come and catch it. They keep it tight for a day or two and leave it in the nearby forests. The terrified monkey does not easily come back into the village after that. That is how it is with anger. You hold on to your anger and refuse to let go of it until you commit enough wrong actions and utter enough wrong words."
— Sri Krishnaji (O1VkNuEChD4, 0s)

golden.query: Why does harboring hurt make us insensitive and blind to the present moment?
golden.answer:
Related, not a direct answer:

"Sometimes happens in life. I have seen people judge themselves for the rest of their lives because of this. At other times, you hurt people with your words and your actions because you get caught in this whirlwind of inner states of anger, violence, fear, hate, and greed. And then you lose control. And in other instances, perhaps you have not hurt others. but you have disappointed yourself with the irresponsibility or save and lethargy whatever it is you need to cross this inner torment and you need to move into a state of forgiveness"
— shared in Times Now (1_-cZz8YRFw, 232s)
